blockers.quote: Day thirty-one. Ten million euros, pouring off your phone.
blockers.why: Check #15 fails: the opening is explicitly a flash-forward teaser rather than the performed arrival of the power.
blockers.fix: Replace lines 17-30 with the chronological midnight rip from 0,01 to 0,02, then reach the thumbnail composition at Lotte's counter within seven seconds. Open narration: "Your phone rips. One cent becomes two." Ask the title question by 0:15.

blockers.quote: Day fifty-six. Jonas pays. He always pays.
blockers.why: Check #12 fails: the final image contains no real line that changes how ordinary money is seen.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "Day fifty-six. Jonas pays. He always pays. A coin isn't a thing. It's Lotte agreeing to bake tomorrow." Then let Jonas's phone rip.

blockers.quote: Anchor: Breaking news. Somewhere in Berlin, one bank account is growing faster than anyone can count.
blockers.why: The "No new person after 60%" check fails: the anchor first appears around 8:00.
blockers.fix: Remove the anchor. Show the alert reaching established characters—Jonas, Lotte and Herr Brandt—and give the news line to the narrator or an on-screen alert.

suggestions.quote: Thirty people ride to the end of the line and back. Because it's free. The whole tram, all day, costs less than tonight will hand you back before breakfast.
suggestions.fix: Escalate beyond the preceding street party: make every tram in Berlin free for an hour, while preserving this tram app as the source of the later one-cent refund.

suggestions.quote: Day thirty-three. Forty million euros. Jonas has a football club. Not supports. Has. The one at the end of the tram line, that loses every Saturday.
suggestions.fix: Replace the familiar billionaire purchase with a doubling-specific failure: buy every seat for Jonas, then show resale prices doubling because seats cannot multiply.

suggestions.quote: And if you never stop? Day two hundred and sixty-seven. More cents in your account than atoms in the observable universe (c12).
suggestions.fix: Tie this image directly to the decision: "Miss midnight, and by day two hundred and sixty-seven the account holds more cents than the universe holds atoms." That turns awe into urgency.

keep.quote: Jonas: I don't know what to do with my hands when they win.
It isn't taken from anyone. Except it is. From everyone. A little. Every night.
